verses.1: Every friend will say: “I also am a close friend.” But there is a friend who is a friend in name only. Is this not a grief even unto death?
verses.2: But a companion and friend may turn into an enemy.
verses.3: O wicked presumption! From what were you created that you would cover the dry land with your malice and deceitfulness?
verses.4: A companion may rejoice with his friend in good times, but in a time of tribulation, he will be an adversary.
verses.5: There is a companion who commiserates with a friend for the sake of the stomach, but he will shield himself from the enemy.
verses.6: You should not forget your friend in your soul, and you should not be unmindful of him in your wealth.
verses.7: Do not choose to consult with someone who waits in ambush for you. And hide your counsel from those who rival you.
verses.8: Every counselor offers advice, but some are counselors only for themselves.
verses.9: Guard your soul from a counselor. And know beforehand what his interests are. For he will form thoughts from his own soul.
verses.10: Otherwise, he may set a signpost in the ground, and he may say to you:
verses.11: “Your own way is good.” But then he will stand at a distance to see what befalls you.
verses.12: Do not discuss holiness with an irreligious man, nor justice with one who is unjust. You should not speak with a woman about her who is a rival, nor with a coward about war, nor with a merchant about exaggeration, nor with a buyer about selling, nor with a spiteful man about giving thanks,
verses.13: nor with the impious about piety, nor with the dishonest about honesty, nor with the field worker about other kinds of work,
verses.14: nor with a worker hired for a year about the end of the year, nor with a lazy servant about great works. You should pay no heed to these persons in any matter of counsel.
verses.15: But be continually with a holy man, with anyone whom you know to observe the fear of God,
verses.16: whose soul is in agreement with your own soul, and who, when you falter in the dark, will share your sorrows.
verses.17: And establish a heart of good counsel within yourself. For there is nothing of greater usefulness to you than this.
verses.18: At any time, the soul of a holy man declares more truths than seven vigilant watchmen sitting in a high place.
verses.19: But concerning all things, pray to the Most High, so that he may direct your way in truth.
verses.20: In all your works, let a true word precede you, with steadfast counsel before every deed.
verses.21: A wicked word can change the heart. From the heart four kinds of things arise: good and evil, life and death. And the tongue is continually their ruler. There is a man who is an astute teacher of many, and yet this is useless to his own soul.
verses.22: A man of experience has taught many, and this is pleasant to his own soul.
verses.23: Whoever speaks mere rhetoric is hateful; he will be deceived in every matter.
verses.24: Grace is not given to him from the Lord. For he has been deprived of all wisdom.
verses.25: There is a wise man who is wise within his own soul, and the fruit of his understanding is praiseworthy.
verses.26: A wise man instructs his own people, and the fruit of his understanding is faithful.
verses.27: A wise man will be filled with blessings, and those who see will praise him.
verses.28: The life of a man is in the number of his days. But the days of Israel are innumerable.
verses.29: A wise man will inherit honor among the people, and his name will live in eternity.
verses.30: Son, test your own mind in your life, and if it is lacking, you should not give it authority.
verses.31: For not all things are fitting for all persons, and not every kind of thing is agreeable to every soul.
verses.32: Do not choose to be eager during any feast, and you should not act with excess toward any food.
verses.33: For in excessive eating there will be infirmity, and gluttony will continue even unto illness.
verses.34: By excessive drinking, many have passed away. But he who abstains will add to his life. [ Sirach 38 ]
